what: Capital One is a US bank built around credit cards. It lends to consumers who use its cards, finances car purchases, takes deposits online, and since buying Discover it also owns a payments network that competes with Visa and Mastercard.
customers: US consumers and small businesses; merchants and card issuers using the Discover network.
money: interest and fees on card balances, plus interchange
car loans and online deposit accounts
moat: Decades of credit data used to price risk, a national deposit base gathered online without branches, and now ownership of a payments network.
risks: Card lending is concentrated in customers whose finances suffer first in a downturn
Charge-offs rise quickly when unemployment increases
Integrating Discover is a large, multi-year undertaking
Regulators scrutinise card fees and late-fee rules
opportunities: Owning the Discover network lets it keep fees that previously went to Visa and Mastercard
Revenue rose about 37% in the last financial year as Discover was consolidated
Cost savings from the merger are still being realised
watch: Net charge-off rates on cards and progress moving its own card volume onto the Discover network.
